html:
The flight of millions of Afghans into Iran after the Soviet invasion of Afghanistan in 1979, which made Iran host to one of the largest refugee populations in the world for decades.

The new Islamic Republic, just born out of the Iranian Revolution, welcomed the refugees as fellow Muslims fleeing an atheist invader. At the peak, around 1990, some three million lived in Iran. Unlike in Pakistan, where most stayed in camps (see Afghan refugees in Pakistan), most lived in cities and worked, often in hard jobs in building and farming. Many were Shia Hazaras and Persian speakers.

More came with the civil war of the 1990s and the rule of the Taliban. Over time Iran's welcome cooled. Rights to school, work and papers were restricted, and there were waves of forced returns, the latest and largest after the Taliban took power again in 2021 and in 2025. A generation of Afghans was born and raised in Iran, and many speak of it as home.
sum: The flight of millions of Afghans into Iran after the Soviet invasion of Afghanistan in 1979, which made Iran host to one of the largest refugee populations in the world for decades.
